title: Seven-day delay bounds crossed zero for six station-adjusted beech leaf-date trends in Germany and Switzerland, 1961-2023
abstract: We tested whether bounded late reporting can change the sign of beech leaf-date time trends in Germany and Switzerland. Six main fits cover 1961-2023 and two separate periods. Models use station intercepts and at least 15 records per station. A zero-to-seven-day delay permits both slope signs in all six fits. Full-period reported slopes are -2.07 and -1.50 days per decade. The smallest caps that permit zero are 6.66 and 5.60 days. With at least 25 records per station, the German full-period range stays negative at seven days. Thus the result depends on coverage. These are exact fixed-record bounds, not confidence intervals or measured errors. No visit history tests the assumed caps. Different phase thresholds, missing records, observer changes and linear time models limit use. We infer no causal climate or pollution effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure support reproduction. External source records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Six main beech leaf-date trends and exact ranges under a delay of zero to seven days. Orange points show reported slopes. Blue bars are sensitivity bounds, not confidence intervals.
